L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal

claims.claim: Alfuzosin, which shares diaminopyrimidine/quinazoline, dimethoxyaryl, and amide motifs with the query, has absolute oral bioavailability of 49% under fed conditions, supporting F >= 20% for this scaffold class.

Colchicine, a methoxy-rich tricyclic amide with P-gp-limited absorption, has mean absolute oral bioavailability around 37-55% across formulations and populations, indicating that high lipophilicity and polar surface area do not preclude F >= 20%.

Indomethacin, an indole/chlorophenyl/methoxy carboxylic acid, has absolute bioavailability of 76-80% in sustained-release form, supporting oral absorption of indole-chlorophenyl-containing structures.

Rigosertib, a methoxy-rich molecule, has absolute oral bioavailability of 34.8-35% in fasted patients, and GDC-0810, a chlorophenyl indole-like molecule, was predicted at about 45%, both above the 20% threshold.
Additional high-F records for omeprazole, loratadine, midodrine, and 5-HTP provide further context that diverse oral drugs exceed 20% despite varying physicochemical properties.

evidence_gaps: No direct query-specific absolute oral bioavailability measurement or IV-referenced AUC comparison is available.
No query-specific solubility, permeability, first-pass metabolism, or efflux data are available; the low prior is physicochemical only.
Structural transfer from analogs is qualitative; no exact match to the query's benzofuran-diaminopyrimidine-indole scaffold is present.
Some positive records come from modified-release, fed, fasted, or disease-specific populations that may not match the query's unstated condition.
GDC-0810 bioavailability is PBPK-predicted rather than clinically measured.
content.decision_summary: All L1 gold records in the transferable contexts report absolute oral bioavailability at or above roughly 35-80%, and none provide affirmative threshold-relevant evidence for F < 20%. The physicochemical low prior is not endpoint proof and is outweighed by consistent high-F analog evidence, so F >= 20% is better supported.
